cards.text: Short one, friend: fourteen verses from John, who calls himself the elder. He's writing to one man, Gaius, whom he calls beloved and says he loves in the truth. I've written longer notes on the back of a takeout menu!

cards.question: John opens by praying that Gaius will prosper and enjoy good health in every way. What does John say is already prospering?

cards.text: Some brothers came to John and testified about Gaius's devotion to the truth, and Gaius is still walking in it. How does John take the news? Like a man who just pulled a PERFECT batch out of the oven.

cards.question: John says he has no greater ___ than to hear that his children are walking in the truth.

cards.text: Then John tells Gaius he's faithful in what he's doing for the brothers. FAITHFUL, friend! I've had oven timers that couldn't make it through one batch.

cards.question: True or false: Gaius already knew these brothers well before he helped them.

cards.text: Those brothers testified to the church about Gaius's love, and friend, that beats any five-star review.

cards.question: What does John say Gaius will do well to do for these brothers?

answers.text: Send them on in a manner worthy of God
Keep them in his own home for good
Bring them before the elders in Jerusalem

cards.question: These brothers went out on behalf of the Name. John says they accepted ___ from the Gentiles.
True or false: John says that supporting men like these makes us fellow workers for the truth.

cards.text: Now the letter turns, friend. John says he wrote to the church about this, but a man named Diotrephes "will not accept our instruction."

cards.question: Diotrephes won't accept the instruction John sent to the church. John says Diotrephes loves to be ___.

cards.text: Loves to be first, like the dead batteries I shared a drawer with, arguing ALL DAY over who had the most charge left. And John says if he comes, he'll call attention to Diotrephes's malicious slander against them.

cards.question: Slander isn't enough for Diotrephes. What does he refuse to do for the brothers?
True or false: Diotrephes lets others in the church welcome the brothers if they want to.
John turns back to Gaius: "Beloved, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good." The one who does good is of God. What does John say about the one who does evil?

answers.text: He has not heard the Word

cards.text: Then John brings up a new name: Demetrius. Different man, VERY different report.

cards.question: Demetrius has a good testimony from everyone, and from the truth itself. True or false: John refuses to add his own testimony for Demetrius.

cards.text: John's got many things left to write, but he'd rather skip the pen and ink and see Gaius soon, face to face. Friend, John is NOT a group chat guy.

cards.question: John signs off wishing Gaius peace and sending greetings from the friends with him. What does he ask Gaius to do for the friends where Gaius is?

answers.text: Greet each of them by name
Send them all to visit John

findings.problem: "I've written longer notes on the back of a takeout menu!" adds to the backstory. He only wrote one note in the drawer, and it was shorter than this letter. "Notes," plural, and "longer" make up a new habit that isn't in his story.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The takeout menu is a small detail from the drawer that the line never explains. A baker who only knows he spent years in a junk drawer won't see why a takeout menu matters, so the joke doesn't land.

rule.text: Bakers know he spent years in a junk drawer, from onboarding. The drawer's small details, like the batteries, the key or the coupon, only come up when the line says what they are, like "the dead batteries I shared that drawer with."

findings.problem: Card 1 names the elder as John. 3 John never names its writer, and no verse supplies a reference for this. Naming John is church tradition, not something the text states.
findings.question: When a letter's author is known by tradition but never named in Scripture, like the elder of 2 and 3 John, may Papa Dorin name the author without a reference? Or should he say only "the elder," as the text does?

findings.problem: The question says "these brothers" but never says who they are. It points back to story cards that are no longer on screen.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The right answer, "Send them on in a manner worthy of God," is the only answer in Bible-sounding wording. It stands out from the two plain wrong answers. Also, no earlier card says the brothers are travelers, so "send them on" can't be reasoned out over "keep them in his own home."

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: "Diotrephes loves to be ___" asks the baker to guess the exact word in the letter. From refusing instruction, "right" or "heard" is just as reasonable as "first." Getting it right comes down to luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card tells "loves to be first," which is from verse 9, and the slander, which is from verse 10. But it cites only 3 John 1:10. It should cite 3 John 1:9-10.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: No card in the stop tells that Diotrephes even puts people out of the church (3 John 1:10). This is the high point of what he does, and the baker never hears it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question gives the first half of John's saying and asks the baker to finish it ("the one who does evil has not seen God"). This is guessing the next words of a line in a letter. No earlier card sets it up, so "has not been forgiven" is just as reasonable a pick.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
